topic: Visit of Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan to Sri Lanka

subtopics.title: Bilateral Ties and Cooperation Areas
subtopics.summary: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan made the first-ever bilateral visit to Sri Lanka and held talks with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo. The visit highlighted trade, development, defence and development-linked cooperation between India and Sri Lanka. India is Sri Lanka's largest trade partner and largest source of tourists.
facts: First-ever bilateral visit to Sri Lanka by the Vice President
Talks with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake held in Colombo
India is Sri Lanka's largest trade partner and largest source of tourists
India-Sri Lanka FTA was signed in 2000
India supports development of Trincomalee as a Regional Energy and Industrial Hub
India and Sri Lanka jointly commission a Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre
Construction of Sampur Solar Power Plant in Sri Lanka
Joint exercises: SLINEX (Naval), MITRA SHAKTI (Army), MILAN (Multi-Lateral Naval)
MoUs under Multi-Sectoral Grant Assistance Programme focus on healthcare and women's empowerment
Sri Lanka joins the International Big Cat Alliance

subtopics.title: Diaspora Schemes: PIO and OCI
subtopics.summary: The OCI scheme was introduced in 2005 through an amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955, and was merged with the PIO scheme in 2015. PIO card holders need no visa to visit India for 15 years from the date of issue of the card. OCI holders get a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa and are exempt from police reporting.
facts: OCI scheme introduced in 2005 via amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955
PIO and OCI schemes merged in 2015
PIO: a foreign citizen, except nationals of Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, China, Iran, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Nepal
PIO: a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in and a permanent resident of India, or the person is a spouse of an Indian citizen or PIO
PIO card holders need no visa for 15 years from the date of issue of the card
PIO stay up to 180 days is exempt from FRRO/FRO registration; longer stays must register within 30 days
OCI eligibility covers persons eligible for Indian citizenship on 26.01.1950 and their minor children
Persons who were ever citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are not eligible for OCI
OCI holders get a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa and are exempt from police reporting
OCI holders have no right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties

subtopics.title: Katchatheevu Island Dispute
subtopics.summary: Katchatheevu is an uninhabited 285-acre island in the Palk Strait, and its ownership remained disputed until 1974. Sri Lanka based its claim on early medieval rule and Portuguese jurisdiction, while India's claim traced control through the Ramnad Zamindari under the Nayak dynasty of Madurai. Tensions over Indian fishermen after the 2009 Sri Lanka Civil War have renewed demands over the island.
facts: Katchatheevu is an uninhabited 285-acre island located in the Palk Strait
The island was once part of the Madras Presidency
Ownership remained a point of dispute between India and Sri Lanka until 1974
Sri Lanka's claim: Jaffna Kingdom ruled the island in the early medieval period
Sri Lanka's claim: Portuguese (1505-1658 CE) exercised jurisdiction over the islet
India's claim: control later shifted to the Ramnad Zamindari under the Nayak dynasty of Madurai in the 17th century
Indo-Sri Lankan Maritime Agreement 1974, under Indira Gandhi, agreed to cede the island to Sri Lanka
The 1974 agreement allowed Indian fishermen continued access to Katchatheevu
Additional Agreement of 1976 barred fishing by both countries in each other's EEZ, with the island at the boundary
After the 2009 Sri Lanka Civil War, arrests and torture allegations of Indian fishermen renewed Katchatheevu demands

subtopics.title: Sri Lanka Profile and Strategic Context
subtopics.summary: Colombo is the executive capital of Sri Lanka and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte houses the legislature, with Harini Amarasuriya as Prime Minister and Anura Kumara Dissanayake as President. The LTTE, formed in 1976, and the 13th Amendment shape Sri Lanka's internal politics. China's growing presence through financial aid and Hambantota Port raises strategic concerns for India.
facts: Capital: Colombo (Executive) and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (Legislature)
PM: Harini Amarasuriya; President: Anura Kumara Dissanayake
Currency: Sri Lankan Rupee
LTTE was formed in 1976 as a self-styled 'National Freedom Movement of People of Tamil Eelam'
LTTE undertook terrorist activities in Sri Lanka, especially against Sinhalese
13th Amendment of the Sri Lankan Constitution led to Provincial Councils with power-sharing for all 9 provinces
China's influence grows through financial aid and Hambantota Port
Chinese vessels Shi Yan-6 and Yuan Wang-5 conduct data collection, potentially supporting military operations against India
Multilateral forums include BIMSTEC, SAARC, Colombo Security Conclave and Indian Ocean Rim Association

quizzes.passage:
Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) are two schemes that link people of Indian heritage living abroad with India. The OCI scheme was introduced through an amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955. The PIO and OCI schemes were later merged into a single arrangement. The booklet presents the two categories side by side under the heading PIO VS OCI.

A foreign citizen can qualify as a PIO if a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in India and was a permanent resident of India. The definition also covers a foreign citizen who is the spouse of a citizen of India or of a PIO, and it carves out exceptions for nationals of certain countries. PIO card holders enjoy parity with NRIs in economic, financial and educational benefits, and any future benefits given to NRIs are also available to PIO card holders.

OCI registration is open to certain foreign nationals with links to India, and minor children of such persons are also eligible. Registered OCI holders receive a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa. This visa allows the holder to visit India at any time, for any length of time and for any purpose.

The booklet sets out who qualifies for each category and what benefits each one provides, with separate sections for each.

quizzes.passage:
The booklet compares two schemes for people of Indian heritage living abroad: the Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) scheme and the Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) scheme. The OCI scheme began as an amendment to the Citizenship Act, and the two schemes were later merged into one arrangement.

A foreign citizen qualifies as a PIO when a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in India and was a permanent resident of India. The definition also covers a foreign citizen who is the spouse of a citizen of India or of a PIO, and it excludes nationals of certain countries. PIO card holders have parity with NRIs in economic, financial and educational benefits.

OCI registration is open to certain foreign nationals with links to India. Minor children of an eligible person are also eligible. OCI holders are exempt from police reporting for any length of stay in the country. They enjoy parity with NRIs in the economic, financial and education fields, but they have no right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties.

The booklet describes both categories with their eligibility and benefits. It presents these rules for each scheme separately, under the heading PIO VS OCI, and lists the benefits of each category in turn.
